Our valued client, West Coast Rewind - based in Malaga WA – is an innovative and professional Electro-Mechanical business established over 25 years. They are looking for ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TECHNICIANS to join their team of professionals on a fulltime and permanent basis.

Position Description & Requirements:
Technically skilled Electronic Engineering Technician to support the manufacturing, servicing, testing, rewinding, and refurbishment of electric motors, generators, and related rotating equipment. Work closely with engineers and technicians to diagnose faults, prepare detailed technical drawings, assist with motor rewinds, and test electrical equipment to ensure compliance with industry standards

Key Responsibilities:
Assist in the inspection, dismantling, and fault analysis of electric motors, generators, transformers, and similar equipment.
Support motor rewind operations by documenting coil data, winding diagrams, and insulation specifications.
Conduct electrical and performance testing (e.g. surge, hipot, resistance, no-load tests) on motors and components.
Assist in the design and setup of test benches and control systems for repaired or rewound motors.
Maintain detailed service and test records for all equipment worked on.
Coordinate with engineers and workshop personnel to ensure repair procedures meet electrical and safety standards.
Provide technical input on materials, processes, and methods for improving reliability and performance.
Ensure all work complies with company safety procedures and industry standards (EASA).

Qualifications:
In depth experience Electrical/Electronic Engineering Technology or a related field.
Knowledge of electric motor construction, operation, and rewinding techniques.
Experience using AutoCAD or similar drafting tools.
Familiarity with test equipment such as multimeters, insulation testers, and surge testers.
Strong technical problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Ability to interpret technical manuals, wiring diagrams, and electrical schematics.
Good communication and teamwork abilities.

Desirable Experience:
Hands-on experience in a motor rewind or electrical repair workshop.
Knowledge of VFDs, soft starters, or motor control circuits.
Familiarity with standards from EASA related to motor repair and testing.

Work Environment:
Workshop and test lab setting.
Occasional on-site motor testing, removal, or installation at client facilities.
Use of PPE and adherence to safety protocols is required

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $75,000 and $80,000 per annum + Super
